A review an earlier release left pending is decided, finalised and recorded on this release's figures; a rule whose figure changed takes its outcome from the stored policy result, else from the policy file with the stored hash.
When neither settles it, cma resume refuses, naming the figure and saying to run cma run again; the stored review is untouched, nothing is recorded, and this is outside R53's guarantee.
The owner's 94ced9c already builds it; before its review T04 catches a refusal raised on the reviewer's answer, stops a stored rule without its comparison from raising, and adds one CLI test.

proposals.text: T04 before its review: catch StaleReviewError (and the refresh's AmountError and ReconciliationError) around _decide's graph.invoke (src/cma/cli.py:289), or hand the review node the policy result cma resume showed, so that a policy file changed or removed while the reviewer answers ends in cma resume's refusal with exit 2, nothing recorded and the review still pending, never a traceback (R53 revision 28).

T04 before its review: in policy._from_stored, a stored rule whose op or threshold is missing (RuleResult defaults, src/cma/models.py:182-183) settles nothing from the stored result and falls to the hash-checked policy file, instead of raising at OPS[op] (src/cma/policy.py:96).

A contracts-marked CLI test for R53's scope: an earlier-release review whose M3 becomes n/a under a custom rule with when_missing: pass, with the policy file moved. cma resume exits 2, its message names M3 and cma run, no --out file or evidence is written, and graph.get_state shows the same interrupt and stored values as before. A second case edits the file instead of moving it.

Revision 28, after D249 (changes requested by the owner on 2026-11-20, given in chat, after T04's twentieth review, verify-146). Only R53 changes; its id, form and risk tag do not. Since T04's sixteenth review, verify-142, `cma resume` decides a review that an earlier release left pending on the figures this release computes. The stored figures came from the earlier release's float arithmetic and hold no total money in or money-in buckets (R1, R2, P2), so the review's policy outcome has to follow the new figures. verify-144, verify-145 and verify-146 each failed R53 on such a review that `cma resume` refused although its outcome might not have changed. In verify-146 a custom rule passed when M3 cannot be computed, M3 became n/a, the stored policy result does not hold that action, and the policy file had been moved. D249 accepts such cases as outside the guarantee, to push development forward, and asks for one scope limit under R53, which R53 now states. A review left pending by an earlier release resumes and is decided, finalised and recorded on the figures this release computes. Where a figure a policy rule reads differs, the rule's outcome comes from the stored policy result when that settles it (the value passes, with or without a referral, or fails a rule it already failed). Otherwise it comes from the policy file the review was drafted with, known by the hash stored with the review. When neither settles it, `cma resume` refuses, naming the figure and saying to run `cma run` on the statement again; the stored review is untouched and nothing is recorded. Resuming a review whose policy outcome cannot be known is outside R53's guarantee, and storing a copy of every policy in the checkpoint is outside this release. Revision 28 makes four readings. First, the stored result settles a rule only where it holds the rule's comparison and limits, from which passing and the referral bands are read, so a stored rule without them settles nothing. Second, a rule whose figure is unchanged keeps its stored outcome, as D249's 'where a figure a policy rule reads differs' implies. Third, the policy file with the stored hash is the policy the stored result came from, so for a rule both settle it gives the same outcome, and a build that evaluates the whole file once it reads it meets R53. Fourth, being decided on this release's figures includes the grounding check: the stored memo is checked against them as any draft is, and approving one that no longer holds needs the grounding override. requirements.md.new:
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep cma run, cma resume, cma import monzo, cma generate, the MCP tools and the evidence JSON working with their current options and fields; new evidence fields SHALL be additive, and every new evidence record SHALL carry a schema version.
Scope (revision 28): a review left pending by an earlier release resumes under cma resume and is decided, finalised and recorded on the figures this release computes from the review's stored lines (R1, R2, P2), never on the figures the earlier release stored. Its stored memo is checked against those figures by the grounding guard, as any draft is. Where the two sets of figures are the same, the review resumes as before. A policy rule whose figure is the same keeps its stored outcome. Where a figure a policy rule reads differs, THE SYSTEM SHALL take that rule's outcome from the stored policy result when the stored result settles it. The stored result settles it when it holds the rule's comparison and limits and the figure's new value passes the rule, with or without a referral, or fails a rule its stored value already failed. Otherwise THE SYSTEM SHALL take the outcome from the policy file the review was drafted with, and SHALL use that file only when its hash is the hash stored with the review. That file is the policy the stored result came from, so it gives the same outcome for every rule the stored result settles, and once THE SYSTEM uses it, it may take every rule's outcome from it. IF neither settles a rule's outcome, because the stored result does not and the policy file is missing, cannot be read or has another hash, or the review stores no hash, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to resume the review, naming at least one figure whose rule neither settles and saying to run cma run on the statement again; SHALL leave the stored review as it was; and SHALL record nothing. Such a refusal keeps this requirement: resuming a review whose policy outcome cannot be known is outside its guarantee, and storing a copy of every policy in the checkpoint is outside this release.
Source: D249 (revision 28: a review left pending by an earlier release resumes and is decided, finalised and recorded on the figures this release computes; where a figure a policy rule reads differs, each rule's outcome comes from the stored policy result when it settles it, and otherwise from the policy file the review was drafted with, known by the hash stored with the review; when neither settles it, cma resume refuses, naming the figure and saying to run cma run on the statement again, with the stored review untouched and nothing recorded).

## Decision
design.md.new:
on every supported Python.

**Sub-decision: a resumed review whose policy outcome the changed figures leave open (revision 28, after verify-144 to verify-146; D249, in R53 since revision 28).** A review that an earlier release left pending holds that release's figures, which can be a penny from the exact pence and lack M17 and the money-in buckets, and a policy result computed from them. Recomputed here, a figure a policy rule reads can move. Where it moves within the rule's band, the stored rule's comparison and limits give its outcome. Where it newly fails or becomes n/a, the outcome needs the rule's fail or when-missing action, which only the policy holds. (i) Resume on the stored figures and the stored result, as before verify-142: verify-141 and verify-142 failed it, since the figures shown and recorded would not be this release's (R1, R2). (ii) Recompute the figures and take each changed rule's outcome from the stored result where it settles it. Otherwise use the policy file the review was drafted with, only if its hash is the stored one. Otherwise refuse, naming the figure and saying to run `cma run` again, with the review left pending and nothing recorded (D249; 94ced9c). (iii) Store a copy of the policy in every new checkpoint, so that a later release can always settle a rule: it does nothing for reviews already pending, which hold no copy, and it adds a field the checkpoint allow-list and every resume carry. (iv) Evaluate with whatever policy file is at the stored path, or the packaged default: the outcome would come from a policy the review was not drafted with, and a file swapped while the review waits would change what is recorded. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer (D249), which R53 states since revision 28. (iii) is outside this release, as D249 says. What (ii) costs: a review cannot be resumed if the earlier release left it pending, its figure newly fails a rule or becomes n/a, and its policy file has moved, changed or was never hashed. The reviewer then drafts again with `cma run`. Once this release rewords R9's description in the packaged policy (Migration), the packaged file's hash changes, so for a review drafted with the packaged policy only the stored result can settle a rule. Each case needs a review left pending across the upgrade and a figure that moves across a rule's edge, as near the import limit or at a rounding midpoint.
